reviews.title: Guinness 0.0
reviews.abv: Marketed as 0.0%; independent testers have reported a detectable ceiling around 0.05%
reviews.dealcoholization_method: Cold filtration after a conventional Guinness brew
reviews.volume: 440 ml can (secondary listing; US cans also appear as 14.9 fl oz)
reviews.summary: A St James's Gate stout with the alcohol filtered out cold. Cream, coffee, and that familiar surge — then a slightly sweeter, lighter finish.

reviews.title: Leitz Eins-Zwei-Zero Riesling
reviews.abv: <0.1% vol (producer); bottling tolerance up to 0.38% vol
reviews.summary: A Rheingau Riesling put through vacuum distillation. Citrus, rhubarb, and a dry-seeming finish — with more residual sugar than the word dry implies.

reviews.title: Lyre's Italian Orange
reviews.summary: A built-from-scratch blood-orange aperitif under 0.3% ABV. Useful in a Negroni-shaped drink. Not wine, not a spirit, not dealcoholized.

reviews.title: Thomson & Scott Noughty Sparkling Chardonnay
reviews.abv: 0.0% vol on producer technical data; some US retailers list <0.5% ABV
reviews.dealcoholization_method: Vacuum distillation with aroma recovery; some trade sheets also name spinning-cone technology
reviews.producer: Thomson & Scott, with dealcoholization associated with Carl Jung
reviews.summary: Organic La Mancha Chardonnay, dealcoholized, then lightly carbonated. Pale, crisp, and modestly sweet — with a documented alcohol-removal step.

reviews.title: Spiritless Kentucky 74
reviews.abv: Typically labeled 0.5% ABV or below; some later brand copy has said under 0.05%
reviews.dealcoholization_method: Reverse distillation after thermal oak extraction in high-proof neutral grain spirit
reviews.summary: Louisville's reverse-distilled whiskey alternative. Alcohol is removed from an oak-charged high-proof spirit. It is not dealcoholized Maker's Mark.
